options.content:
# VoltDB configuration

Below's information comes from @SystemInformation call, for detailed description please go to [documentation](https://docs.voltdb.com/UsingVoltDB/sysprocsysteminfo.php#sysprocsysinforetvalovervw).

panels.description: The VoltDB software version this cluster is running. Check it when confirming an upgrade took effect or when matching observed behavior to a specific release.
panels.title: Version

panels.description: How long the cluster has been running since it last started. A sudden drop back toward zero means the cluster was restarted.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: The cluster's current operating state. RUNNING is normal; PAUSED means client transactions are blocked (typically during maintenance); INITIALIZING and SHUTTINGDOWN appear briefly during startup and shutdown.
panels.title: Cluster state

panels.description: Whether the cluster currently holds all its redundant copies of data. FULL means every partition has its full set of copies available; REDUCED means one or more copies are missing (usually a node is down), leaving less headroom before further failures put data at risk.
panels.title: Cluster safety

panels.description: The number of nodes the cluster is configured to run with. Compare it against the current node count to see whether any nodes are missing.
panels.title: Full cluster size

panels.description: The number of nodes currently active in the cluster. If this is below the configured (full) cluster size, one or more nodes are down.
panels.title: Current size

panels.description: Key identity settings for the cluster: the exact software build it is running, its cross-datacenter replication role, and whether it is deployed on Kubernetes.
panels.title: Configuration overview

panels.description: The number of redundant copies kept of each partition (K-safety). A value of 0 means no redundancy, so losing a single node halts the cluster; a higher value lets the cluster survive that many simultaneous node failures.
panels.title: kFactor

panels.description: The number of physical CPU cores on the host. Useful for capacity planning and for confirming nodes are running on the expected hardware.
panels.title: CPU Cores

panels.description: The number of hardware processor threads on the host. Useful for capacity planning and for confirming nodes match their expected hardware.
panels.title: CPU Threads

panels.description: The identifier assigned to this cluster for cross-datacenter replication (DR). Use it to tell paired clusters apart when replication is configured.
panels.title: Cluster id

panels.description: The number of execution sites (partitions) each node runs. Together with the node count and K-safety, this determines how the workload is spread across the cluster.
panels.title: sites per host

panels.description: The cluster's main deployment settings in one place: its replication role and priority, whether export, network partition detection, and metrics collection are turned on, the heartbeat timeout, the pace allowed for elastic rebalancing when nodes are added or removed, and the memory, temp-table, and replication buffer limits. Review these to confirm the running configuration matches what was intended.

elasticduration.text: target duration of rebalance transactions in milliseconds

elasticthroughput.text: target throughput of rebalance transactions in MB/second

temptablesmaxsize.text: maximum size of the temp tables

targets.expr: max (voltdb_systeminformation_deployment_info{v2="1", namespace="$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}) by (drpriority,drrole, elasticduration, elasticthroughput, export, heartbeattimeout, partitiondetection, prioritiesenabled, temptablesmaxsize, metrics, memorylimit, drconsumermaxbuffers, drconsumermaxbytes)

panels.title: Deployment configuration

panels.description: Command logging settings: whether it is enabled, the mode (synchronous or asynchronous), the disk space reserved for command logs (in MB), and how often data is flushed to disk - both by time (in milliseconds) and by number of transactions.

commandlogfreqtime.text: frequency of cmd logging in milliseconds

commandlogfreqtxns.text: frequency of cmd logging in number of transactions

commandlogmode.text: cmd logging mode, sync or async

targets.expr: max (voltdb_systeminformation_commandlog_info{v2="1", namespace="$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}) by (commandlogenabled, commandlogfreqtime, commandlogfreqtxns, commandlogmode, commandlogsize)

panels.title: Command Log Configuration

panels.description: Automatic snapshot settings: whether periodic snapshots are enabled, how often they are taken, how many are kept, and the priority given to snapshot work. Use this to confirm the cluster is taking regular on-disk backups.

targets.expr: max (voltdb_systeminformation_snapshot_info{v2="1", namespace="$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}) by (snapshotenabled, snapshotfrequency, snapshotpriority, snapshotretain)

panels.title: Snapshot configuration

panels.description: Time left before the current license expires. Plan a renewal well before this reaches zero to avoid running on an expired license.
panels.title: License expires in

panels.description: The calendar date on which the current license expires.
panels.title: License expires on

panels.description: The maximum number of nodes the current license permits. "Limit not relevant" means the license does not cap the node count.
panels.title: Host count limit

panels.description: The maximum number of processor cores the current license permits. "Limit not relevant" means the license does not cap the core count.
panels.title: Cores count limit

panels.description: The maximum Java memory (heap) the VoltDB server is allowed to use, set when the server starts. If usage approaches this limit the server can pause or run out of memory.
panels.title: Max Java heap
